Maintenance SOP

Ongoing maintenance schedule, how to handle tool drift, context updates, pipeline re-runs, and the knowledge base update cycle.
Admin / Power Users Only
In This Guide

Most of this system is low-maintenance by design. The automated tasks run on their own. The tools only need attention when something changes (new knowledge, a broken behavior, a new project) or on the quarterly review cycle. You are not babysitting this daily.
Maintenance Schedule
A reference for what needs to happen and how often. Most tasks are triggered by an event, not a calendar date.

Review flags and take action on any red or amber items - open System Monitor Navigator to get specifics. 5 min review; variable if action needed

Handling Tool Drift
Tool drift happens when a project's behavior starts diverging from what it was designed to do - either because the instructions have gaps that real-world use exposed, or because supporting context (like the knowledge base) changed. Here is how to identify and fix it.
🚫
Hard drift - act immediately
The tool consistently gives wrong answers on a specific type of question. Multiple people report the same issue. The tool is missing a behavior that it had before. A critical workflow is broken.
⚠️
Soft drift - address this week
One or two users mention the tool "seems off." Responses are still in the right direction but less precise than they used to be. The tool handles the core case well but struggles on edge cases.
🔧 How to fix drift

0. Log it first. As soon as you notice bad behavior, trigger the Agent Quality Logger skill: "log this feedback" or "that was wrong." It takes 60 seconds and captures the issue in feedback-log.md before you forget the details. Critical-severity issues prompt immediate routing. Others are surfaced in Monday's System Monitor report.

1. Reproduce it. Open the tool and ask it the exact question or do the exact task that is failing. Copy the bad response.

2. Open The Architect and trigger Project Feedback. Describe exactly what went wrong, what the tool said, and what the correct behavior should be. Project Feedback will read the current instructions and produce an exact-text fix - not a vague suggestion.

Prompt format:
Fix my project. Blueprint at project-blueprints/[project-name]/. Issue: [describe what the tool did wrong]. The correct behavior should be: [describe what it should have done]. Here is the actual bad response: [paste it].

3. Apply the fix. Project Feedback will give you the exact text to add, remove, or replace in instructions.md. Make the change in the file AND re-paste the updated instructions into the live workspace/project.

4. Increment the version. Update the version number in handoff.md (v1.0 - v1.1 - etc.) and note what changed.

5. Re-run Run Test Cases. Confirm the fix worked and did not break anything that was previously passing.

6. Training doc drift is handled automatically. When The Architect's own instructions.md is updated, or another flagship project's instructions.md changes, The Architect runs a training doc drift check as part of the standard process - scanning Training Materials for affected references and auto-applying clear-drift fixes (rename passes, path corrections, callout updates). It surfaces only judgment-call drift to Adam (structural rewrites, contested changes). No manual maintenance pass is required for routine drift.

Updating Project Context
Context files are the documents uploaded to a project that give it School Tech-specific knowledge. They need to be updated when the information they contain changes.
1
Identify which context files need updating
Check context-shared/context-registry.md for a list of all context files, which projects use them, and when they were last updated. The Knowledge Base Update Checker runs weekly and flags files that may be stale.
2
Update the file content
Open the context file and update the relevant sections. Use the Work Personal Assistant to help draft new sections if needed - paste in the source material and ask it to format it consistently with the existing file.
3
Re-upload to all affected projects
For each project listed in the context registry for that file, go to the project settings and replace the old version of the context file with the updated one. Claude.ai and Cowork do not auto-sync context files - you have to do this manually.
Check context-registry.md for the full list of which projects use which files. Do not miss one - a project with stale context will answer incorrectly even if its instructions are fine.
4
Update the registry
Update the "Last Updated" date in context-registry.md for the file you changed.
Re-running the Pipeline on Existing Projects
Quarterly, run Run Test Cases against all active team-facing projects. This catches instruction decay - where behaviors that once passed start failing due to accumulated small changes or context updates.
🔬 Quarterly pipeline re-run process

1. List active projects. Open context-agent-registry.md (workspace root) and identify all projects with Status = Active that are deployed to Claude.ai or Both (team-facing).

2. Run Run Test Cases on each one. Open The Architect (or any Cowork session with the run-test-cases skill enabled) and run a batch test for each project. Save the new report - it supersedes the previous one.

Prompt:
Test my project. The blueprint is at project-blueprints/[project-name]/. Run all 10 test cases in batch mode and give me a full pass/fail report. Save the report as project-blueprints/[project-name]/test-report-[today's date].md

3. Fix any failures. For any project scoring below 8/10, run Project Feedback on the failures. Apply fixes, increment versions, re-test to confirm.

Prioritize team-facing projects. Failures in AI Advisor, STA Support Chat, STA Salesforce Cohort, or STA Main Chat (once Active) affect the cohort directly. Adam-only Cowork projects (Salesforce Admin Assistant, STA Support Expert, etc.) only affect Adam and can wait for the next available window.
Backup and version history: The workspace folder is automatically backed up to GitHub via Obsidian Git every 30 minutes. The repository is at github.com/abaker421/school-tech-ai-system (private). Obsidian must be open and running for the backup interval to fire. To recover a lost file, clone the repo or browse the commit history on GitHub. To roll back a specific file, find the last good commit on GitHub and copy the file contents.
Knowledge Base Update Cycle
The knowledge base underpins the content that AI tools reference when answering School Tech-specific questions. Keeping it current is what keeps the tools accurate over time.
1
Monday morning - check the automated update alert
The Knowledge Base Update Checker runs every Monday at 8:09 AM and sends an email if anything may be stale. Review the output. If no update is flagged, no action needed.
2
If an update is flagged - determine scope
Open Deep Research and ask it to investigate what changed. Feed it the source material (Skyward release notes, updated policies, product changes) and ask it to identify what in the knowledge base is now outdated.
Deep Research has access to the knowledge base index and can identify which modules need updating without you having to review the whole thing.
3
Update the affected knowledge modules
Use the knowledge-base-context-builder skill (via any Cowork session with the skill enabled - typically The Architect) to reformat updated content into the correct module structure. Save the updated modules to the knowledge base folder.
4
Re-upload context files to affected projects
Replace the outdated context files in any project that uses them. Update knowledge-base/index.md with the new last-updated dates.
Warning Signs That Something Needs Attention
These are the signals that should prompt immediate action, not a wait-for-the-next-review response.
Multiple users report the same wrong behavior from the same tool
One report might be user error. Two or more with the same failure pattern means the tool has a real issue.
Action: run Project Feedback, apply fix, re-test, redeploy same day.
A tool starts confidently giving outdated School Tech information
Usually means a knowledge base module is stale after a product update or policy change. The tool does not know the info changed - it answers from what it has.
Action: identify the stale module, update it, re-upload context files to affected projects.
A project's instructions.md and the live workspace instructions do not match
Means a fix was applied to the workspace but not saved back to the file, or vice versa. The file and the live tool have diverged - next time the file is used as a reference, the fix will be lost.
Action: decide which version is correct, update the other to match.
A project in the registry has no test-report file or a test report older than 6 months
The project may never have been formally validated, or it has not been tested since significant changes were made.
Action: add to the next quarterly pipeline re-run queue, or run Run Test Cases on it this week if it is a team-facing tool.
Low-maintenance is a feature, not an accident. This system was built to need minimal daily oversight. If you find yourself doing constant manual correction on a tool's output, that's a signal to fix the underlying instructions or context - not to keep correcting. Run Project Feedback on the tool and apply the root-cause fix. Repeated manual correction is the most common indicator that real maintenance work is overdue.
